name: execa-structured-lifecycle-events
instr:
Consumers building progress UIs and audit logs currently have to coordinate Execa's output, IPC, and settlement surfaces themselves. Add an opt-in typed event feed that exposes a complete buffered subprocess lifecycle without changing normal result behavior.

Add async-only option `events`, accepting exactly `false` (default), `true`, or a selection object containing only the optional boolean keys `{stdout?, stderr?, ipc?}`. Validate it during option normalization: `null`, other primitive values, non-boolean selection values, and unknown keys must throw a `TypeError` whose message mentions `events`, before a child can spawn. Enabled subprocesses expose `subprocess.events`, an async-iterable hub. Every iterator—including late and multiple readers—receives the complete immutable sequence from the beginning. Iteration ends normally after the subprocess fails (for example with a nonzero exit code); awaiting the subprocess retains current resolve/reject semantics. Sync methods, including `execaSync` and `$.sync`, reject the option before spawning with a `TypeError` whose message mentions both `events` and sync execution. Disabled subprocesses expose no event hub.

Every event has zero-based monotonic `sequence` and a discriminating `type`. The first `spawn` event includes `pid`, `command`, `escapedCommand`, and `cwd`.
